metadata.note: The Minnesota and International Railway ('Mike and Ike'), Brainerd - Bemidji - International Falls, with its predecessor the Brainerd and Northern Minnesota and its successor the Northern Pacific. Drawn from research/branches/minnesota_and_international_railway.txt in the site repo (DanielMConnolly/historical-trains) (2026-11-03). Before this layer the map drew no part of this road. Only the report's drawable spans are drawn. Rule 4 splits: B&NM -> M&I on 16/17 July 1900; M&I -> NP on 22 Oct 1941 (all three share identical geometry where they overlap). Not splits: NP stock control of the M&I (the M&I ran its own trains), and the Big Fork and International Falls Railway's ownership of Grand Falls - International Falls (leased to and operated by the M&I from opening). Each M&I section is its own feature because each opened in a different year: Brainerd - Walker 1900 (company start), Walker - Bemidji 1902, Bemidji - Northome 1903, Northome - Ripple 1906, Ripple - International Falls 1908.

not_yet_sourced: Start years that are the first CONFIRMED year, not a known start ([OPEN]): B&NM Brainerd - Walker 1896 (maybe 1893-95), Walker - Bemidji 1902 (track Dec 1898), Bemidji - Northome 1903 (bracket 1901-1903), Ripple - International Falls 1908 (silver spike Sept 1907).
End year that is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end ([OPEN]): Bullhead Lake Branch (Funkley - Kelliher) 1922; could have run to 1941 or later.
NP passenger end 1966 rests on TrailLink alone (28 July 1966, RDC); 1956 is the last independently confirmed year.
Whether NP through trains (later Nos. 11/12) ran over the M&I as NP trains before 1941, which would move the M&I -> NP colour split earlier.
Ripple mileage: 1905 press Northome - Ripple 33 mi vs mileposts about 30; and Ripple's exact site (drawn 1 mi south of Big Falls).
Every headway and avg_speed_kmh except the 1951 NP daily train is an estimate.
branches_deliberately_omitted: B&NM Walker - Bemidji 1899-1900: track complete Dec 1898, but the only passenger evidence is TrailLink's general statement (secondary source only); omitted under the governing principle, so Walker - Bemidji is drawn from 1902 under the M&I.
NP Bullhead Lake Branch (Funkley - Kelliher) after 1941: no NP-era passenger year found (drawable NONE).
Gull River and Northern (Minnesota Logging Railroad) 3 ft gauge line from the Gull River sawmill, 1889-1892: no passenger evidence (drawable NONE).
NP's own Little Falls - Brainerd line, over which Nos. 11/12 ran St. Paul - International Falls: outside this report; no feature in data/ draws it.
The last ~1 mi into the NP Brainerd depot over NP trackage rights: not drawn, to avoid overdrawing the NP Duluth - Staples main.
freight_only_excluded: B&NM / Gull River and Northern logging spurs and temporary branches (~40 mi around 1896): log haulage, no passenger evidence.
Brainerd - International Falls 1966-1985: freight only under NP/BN after the last RDC; BN abandoned the line in 1985 (last train Bemidji - Brainerd 15 Aug 1985).
Funkley - Kelliher after its unknown passenger end: freight until 1985.

The Brainerd end stops at the M&I's junction with the Northern Pacific at the west end of the NP Mississippi River bridge; trains ran about 1 mi further into the NP's Brainerd depot over NP trackage rights, not drawn so as not to overdraw the NP Duluth - Staples feature. segments.note: Brainerd - Merrifield - Nisswa - Pequot - Pine River - Backus - Hackensack - Leech Lake Bridge - Walker. The B&NM (the standard-gauged successor of the 1889 narrow-gauge Gull River and Northern logging road, renamed 16 May 1892) printed a passenger station list in the 1896 Official Guide; TrailLink says it carried over 25,000 passengers a year around 1898-1900, boarding at NP's Brainerd depot via NP trackage rights. 1896 is the earliest CONFIRMED passenger year, NOT a known start [OPEN]: the southern end was standard-gauged early 1893 and may have carried passengers before 1896, but no source proves it. Do not extend earlier without evidence. Ends 1900 because the Minnesota and International took the road over on 16/17 July 1900; service continued under the M&I. The B&NM's Walker - Bemidji extension (track to Bemidji Dec 1898) is NOT drawn for B&NM years: the only evidence of passenger trains on it before 1902 is TrailLink's general passenger figure. Headway is an estimate (about one train each way a day) and is NOT sourced.
sources: Segment-level: 1896 start = branchline.uk's 1896 Official Guide station-name citations (Merrifield, Pequot, Mildred, Lothrop, Leech Lake Bridge), as read by the research report; 1900 end = M&I takeover 16/17 July 1900 per TrailLink. Headway and avg_speed_kmh NOT SOURCED.

segments.note: The former B&NM main line, run by the Minnesota and International ('Mike and Ike') from its takeover on 16/17 July 1900 until the Northern Pacific took over all M&I assets on 22 Oct 1941. The NP held financial control of the M&I from early on (a controlling interest by WWI per TrailLink), but contemporary papers call these 'M. & I.' trains under an M&I superintendent, so the M&I is treated as the operator until 1941 (open question: whether pre-1941 Guides printed NP through trains Nos. 11/12 over the M&I as NP trains, which would move this split earlier). Lake-resort ('Lake Park Region') traffic was heavy until the 1920s. Headway is an estimate (about one train each way a day) and is NOT sourced.
sources: Segment-level: 1900 start and 1941 end are the company changes (TrailLink); M&I passenger trains on the line in 1909 per the Bemidji Daily Pioneer 5 Jan 1909, as read by the research report. Headway and avg_speed_kmh NOT SOURCED.

The Bemidji Daily Pioneer of 13 Dec 1905 reported the extension to Ripple complete, with passenger traffic to begin on Christmas Day 1905 (an announcement, not proof); a 1906 company timetable has trains terminating at Ripple, so 1906 is the first CONFIRMED year. Ripple - Big Falls (about 1 mi) opened with the BF&IF extension in 1907 and is drawn in the Big Falls - International Falls feature instead. Mileage conflict recorded, not resolved: the 1905 press says Northome - Ripple 33 mi, the mileposts about 30. Ends 1941 when the NP took over. Headway is an estimate (about one train each way a day) and is NOT sourced.

segments.note: Funkley (wye on the main line) - Shooks - Kelliher. Mixed trains count as passenger service (Rule 1). 1907 is the first CONFIRMED year (Bemidji Daily Pioneer 28 Dec 1907: 'the Kelliher-Funkley mixed train'); the branch appears with passenger stations in 1904 Rand McNally names, so service probably began earlier. In Oct 1909 a through 'Brainerd-Kelliher M. I. passenger train' ran; in Dec 1919 a passenger train normally ran, with a coach on the freight during the coal strike. The END is the last CONFIRMED year, NOT a known end [OPEN]: two Kelliher teachers 'left Kelliher on the train' in Mar 1922, and the newspaper run consulted ends in the early 1920s, so silence after 1922 is a coverage gap, not evidence of an end. Do not extend without evidence. Freight continued until 1985 (context only); no NP-era passenger year is known, so no NP feature is drawn for the branch. Headway is an estimate (about one train each way a day) and is NOT sourced.
